summary: Backend-only testing for the new admin photo-reel features (reorder + crop) and the hardened gallery upload. Authored /app/backend/tests/test_photo_reel_crop.py with 10 new tests covering all 11 acceptance criteria from the review request. Full backend regression: 50/50 PASSED across test_photo_reel_crop.py (10 new) + test_marketing.py (18) + test_push.py (15) + test_marketing_timezone.py (4) + test_push_health.py (3). The new file snapshots the existing reel state and restores it in module teardown; gallery photos created during the run are removed via DELETE /admin/gallery-photo. HEIC test uses pillow_heif.register_heif_opener() to encode a real HEIF file before upload. Crop-flow test uploads a real source photo, requests a 400x300 crop into slot 2, confirms the JPEG is written to /app/static/gallery/, the file is exactly 400x300, and the reel slot is updated to the new URL — then restores the original reel order.

minor.issue: File cleanup branch only triggers when photo_url starts with '/static/gallery/' or '/files/gallery/'. Modern uploads return URLs like '{REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL}/api/images/gallery/<file>.jpg', which fall into the else branch where file_path = photo_url.replace('{backend_url}/files','/app/static'). Since the URL contains '/api/images/' not '/files', the replace is a no-op and os.path.exists fails silently. Result: DB row is deleted but the JPEG remains on disk forever (small leak). Pre-existing — not introduced by this PR but exposed by the new gallery_crop_ files.

action_items: (Minor) Fix DELETE /api/admin/gallery-photo file-deletion branch to handle the modern '{BACKEND_URL}/api/images/gallery/<filename>' URL format. Current code only cleans '/static/gallery/' or '/files/gallery/' prefixes, so cropped/uploaded JPEGs accumulate on disk despite successful API responses.
critical_code_review_comments: crop_reel_photo blindly trusts c.x/c.y/c.width/c.height as ints with no minimum bound; negative width/height are clamped via max(left+1, ...) but a payload like x=10000,y=10000 on a 100x100 image becomes a 1x1 crop silently. Consider returning 400 if the requested rect doesn't actually overlap the source.

crop_reel_photo's remote-fetch fallback uses urllib.request.urlopen without a User-Agent or scheme allow-list — it will happily fetch arbitrary HTTPS URLs. If photo_url is ever reachable from the public web this is a small SSRF surface. Restrict to URLs starting with REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL or whitelist the gallery prefix.

ReelReorderPayload accepts photos: List[Optional[str]] with no per-item validation. A caller could submit 6 random non-URL strings and they'd be persisted. At minimum reject items that aren't None and don't start with http/https.

Both new endpoints rely on the global cookie middleware for auth (no per-route Depends). That works today, but if the middleware's exempt list grows or the path is renamed, both endpoints become unauthenticated. Consider adding require_admin Depends explicitly for defense-in-depth.

Inline imports inside upload_gallery_photo and crop_reel_photo (PIL, BytesIO, pillow_heif, urllib) repeat on every call. Move to module-level imports — sub-millisecond win and clearer dependency graph.
server.py is now ~3816 lines (per earlier iter notes ~3695 → grew). Photo-reel handlers + Pydantic models could live in a routers/photo_reel.py extracted module.

All 4 are removed via DELETE /admin/gallery-photo and the reel is restored in module teardown — but note the DELETE-endpoint disk-cleanup bug above means the JPEG files remain on /app/static/gallery/ even though their DB rows are gone.

Both require admin_session cookie via the existing global middleware. Hardened upload adds HEIC/HEIF support (pillow_heif==1.3.0) and EXIF transpose + auto-resize to 2000px max edge.
